patch_description: The prior programs that scored 0 all suffered from fragile code paths (placeholder points, exception fallbacks yielding degenerate lattices with collinear triplets). The best performer (0.31) used gradient-informed "perpendicular escape" moves on the worst triplet. I build on that insight but make it robust and stronger: (1) multiple deterministic symmetric seed layouts polished in parallel with the best kept; (2) vectorized min-area computation over all 165 triplets; (3) for the worst triplet, move its points along the exact analytic direction perpendicular to the opposite edge (which provably increases that triplet's area), trying all-subset moves with adaptive step; (4) periodic random-restart perturbation escape from local optima; (5) strict validity guard — the output always has 11 finite, distinct, in-triangle points, with a safe hand-built fallback that itself has decent min-area. This combines the multistart robustness idea with the directed-move idea while eliminating the failure modes that zeroed out earlier scores.
